title: Graded comparison for convolution tensor of filtered K-flat complexes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P,Q$ be integer cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with finite decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Assume that each module $P^n,(F^iP)^n,(\operatorname{gr}^iP)^n,Q^n,(F^jQ)^n,(\operatorname{gr}^jQ)^n$ is flat (its tensor functor preserves exact sequences), and that each complex $P,F^iP,\operatorname{gr}^iP,Q,F^jQ,\operatorname{gr}^jQ$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]; graded complexes mean successive quotients [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. On the total tensor complex $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to ordinary modules by using the one-point site with ring $R$, define the convolution filtration by
$$G^aT=\sum_{i+j=a}\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(F^iP\otimes_R F^jQ)\longrightarrow T\bigr).$$
This is a finite filtration, its underlying, step and graded modules are flat, and its underlying, step and graded complexes are K-flat. There are canonical isomorphisms of cochain complexes
$$\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R\operatorname{gr}^jQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}^a_G T.$$
They are induced by tensoring representatives in filtration steps and then taking their class modulo $G^{a+1}$, and are natural simultaneously for filtration-preserving chain maps in both variables. Consequently they give natural isomorphisms in $D(R)$
$$\operatorname{gr}^a_G T\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jQ,$$
where the ordinary K-flat derived tensor is that of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $A=R$; the underlying $T$ represents $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$. If $u:P\to P'$ and $v:Q\to Q'$ are filtered quasi-isomorphisms between complexes satisfying these same hypotheses, then $\operatorname{Tot}(u\otimes v)$ is a filtered quasi-isomorphism. Here filtered quasi-isomorphism means quasi-isomorphism on every graded complex. All displayed comparisons are compatible with composition and identities. No spectral sequence, truncation filtration or Tor-of-cohomology formula is asserted.

proof.text: We first record the elementary module consequences needed below, with flat meaning exactness of tensor as in the hypotheses. Tensor commutes with direct sums: the inverse to the distribution map sends a pure tensor with a finite-support vector to the finite sum of its component tensors; the two composites are identities on pure tensors. Thus direct sums of exact sequences are exact, by checking kernels and lifting finitely many nonzero components, and direct sums of flat modules are flat. Tensor products of flat modules are flat, since their tensor functor is the composite of two exact tensor functors, under $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$. For $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ with $A,C$ flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] gives a short exact row after tensoring with any module. For an injection $X\hookrightarrow Y$, form these rows for $X,Y$. If an element of $X\otimes B$ dies in $Y\otimes B$, its image in $X\otimes C$ is zero by flatness of $C$; lift it to $X\otimes A$, whose image in $Y\otimes A$ is zero since the bottom row is injective at its first term. Flatness of $A$ kills the lift. Hence tensoring with $B$ preserves injections. Tensor is right exact because balanced maps out of a cokernel tensor correspond exactly to balanced maps annihilating the defining image; consequently $B$ is flat. In particular all modules $P^r/F^iP^r$ and $Q^s/F^jQ^s$ are flat: induct on the finite number of graded layers, starting from the zero quotient at a lower filtration bound, using $0\to\operatorname{gr}^iP^r\to P^r/F^{i+1}P^r\to P^r/F^iP^r\to0$, and the corresponding sequence for $Q$. More precisely, for $i\le A_P$ the quotient $P^r/F^iP^r$ is zero. Induct for $A_P\le i<B_P$ through the displayed short exact sequences; for $i\ge B_P$ the quotient is $P^r$, already assumed flat. The identical argument covers every $j$ for $Q$. Zero modules are flat since their tensor functor is zero.

proof.text: Choose integers $A_P<B_P$ and $A_Q<B_Q$ with $F^{A_P}P=P$, $F^{B_P}P=0$, $F^{A_Q}Q=Q$, $F^{B_Q}Q=0$, using [def-sp-filtration]. The tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] sends $x\otimes y$ with $x\in F^iP^r$, $y\in F^jQ^s$ to $dx\otimes y+(-1)^r x\otimes dy$ in the same filtration pair. Thus each image and its sum $G^a$ is a subcomplex. A summand indexed by $(i,j)$ with $i+j=a+1$ is contained in that indexed by $(i-1,j)$ for $G^a$, so the filtration is decreasing. We have $G^{A_P+A_Q}T=T$, since $(A_P,A_Q)$ contributes all of $T$, and $G^{B_P+B_Q-1}T=0$, since every pair with this sum has $i\ge B_P$ or $j\ge B_Q$. Hence it is a finite filtration, uniformly in the cochain degree.

proof.text: Fix $a$. For each $i+j=a$ project $T$ to $U_{ij}=\operatorname{Tot}((P/F^{i+1}P)\otimes_R(Q/F^{j+1}Q))$. Only finitely many $U_{ij}$ can be nonzero: $i<A_P$ or $j<A_Q$ makes one quotient zero. Restrict these projections to $G^aT$ and combine them into a map to their finite direct sum. On the image of $\operatorname{Tot}(F^rP\otimes F^sQ)$ with $r+s=a$, every component except $(i,j)=(r,s)$ vanishes: otherwise $r>i$ or $s>j$, so one factor projects to zero. Its diagonal component has image $C_{rs}=\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{gr}^rP\otimes\operatorname{gr}^sQ)$. This image identifies with $C_{rs}$ as a subcomplex of $U_{rs}$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to\operatorname{gr}^rP^k\to P^k/F^{r+1}P^k\to P^k/F^rP^k\to0$ and its $Q$ analogue; the quotients are flat by Step 1. Tensoring the two injections successively and taking direct sums over cochain degrees preserves injections. The same lemma, applied to the step/graded short exact sequences, identifies the kernel of the diagonal surjection $\operatorname{Tot}(F^rP\otimes F^sQ)\to C_{rs}$ with the sum of the images of $\operatorname{Tot}(F^{r+1}P\otimes F^sQ)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(F^rP\otimes F^{s+1}Q)$. Explicitly, first quotient the first factor, whose kernel is $F^{r+1}P\otimes F^sQ$; then quotient the second factor, whose kernel is $\operatorname{gr}^rP\otimes F^{s+1}Q$, the image of $F^rP\otimes F^{s+1}Q$. All these assertions hold termwise and their maps commute with the signed tensor differential. The same flat-quotient lemma applied to $0\to F^rP^k\to P^k\to P^k/F^rP^k\to0$ and to $Q$ also shows that the step tensor complexes embed in $T$; however the image formulation in the statement already suffices for the argument. When a diagonal quotient is zero, its entire step tensor lies in the kernel just computed, so no index outside the finite nonzero graded range is discarded without accounting for its contribution.

proof.text: The map of Step 3 therefore factors as a surjection $\rho_a:G^aT\to\bigoplus_{i+j=a}C_{ij}$. Every $C_{ij}$ is reached by lifting tensors to $F^iP\otimes F^jQ$, so it is surjective in every cochain degree. It kills $G^{a+1}$: for a generator with filtration indices $r+s=a+1$ and any $i+j=a$, one has $r>i$ or $s>j$. Conversely write an element of $\ker\rho_a$ as a finite sum of contributions $z_{ij}$ from the diagonal step tensors. By off-diagonal vanishing, the $(i,j)$ component of its image is precisely the graded image of $z_{ij}$. Each is zero, so the kernel calculation of Step 3 puts each contribution in $G^{a+1}$. Thus $\ker\rho_a=G^{a+1}$. By the quotient definition [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], $\rho_a$ induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}^a_GT\simeq\bigoplus_{i+j=a}C_{ij}$. Its inverse sends the tensor of two residue classes to the class in $G^a/G^{a+1}$ of their tensor of representatives. Replacing a representative by a next-step element changes this by an element of $G^{a+1}$, so this is exactly the claimed canonical map.

proof.text: Step 1 and the comparison of Step 4 show that the terms of $T$ and of each $\operatorname{gr}^a_GT$ are flat: each is a direct sum of tensor products of flat modules. Descending from the upper zero tail in Step 2 along $0\to G^{a+1}T^n\to G^aT^n\to(\operatorname{gr}^a_GT)^n\to0$, the flat-extension argument of Step 1 shows that every $G^aT^n$ is flat. Next, total tensor products of K-flat complexes are K-flat directly from [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]: for acyclic $E$, $E\otimes(P\otimes Q)\cong(E\otimes P)\otimes Q$ is acyclic by applying K-flatness first to $P$ and then to $Q$. The associator reindexes the direct sums indexed by triples and sends $(e\otimes p)\otimes q$ to $e\otimes(p\otimes q)$; the coefficients in the differential on the three factors are $1,(-1)^{\deg e},(-1)^{\deg e+\deg p}$ on both sides [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For each $i,j$ and acyclic $E$, the complex $E\otimes\operatorname{gr}^iP$ is acyclic by K-flatness of $\operatorname{gr}^iP$; tensoring it with the K-flat $\operatorname{gr}^jQ$ remains acyclic. The associator just described identifies this result with $E\otimes C_{ij}$, so $C_{ij}$ is K-flat. Finite direct sums of K-flat complexes are K-flat, since tensor distributes over them and their cycles and boundaries are the corresponding finite sums. Thus $T$ and every $\operatorname{gr}^a_GT$ are K-flat. Finally take any acyclic $E$ and tensor each step/graded short exact sequence with it. The graded terms are flat, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective], followed by direct sums over the tensor degrees, makes this a degreewise short exact sequence of total tensor complexes. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] implies that acyclicity of the first and third implies acyclicity of the middle. Finite descending induction from the zero upper tail proves $E\otimes G^aT$ acyclic for every $a$, hence every step is K-flat.

proof.text: For filtered chain maps $u:P\to P'$ and $v:Q\to Q'$, the tensor map sends $G^aT$ into $G^aT'$ because it sends each image for $(i,j)$ into the corresponding image. On the graded comparison of Step 4 the two composites send $[x]\otimes[y]$ to $[u(x)\otimes v(y)]$. These tensors generate, proving simultaneous naturality, including identities and composition. Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $A=R$ to the identity K-flat resolutions of $P$ and of each $\operatorname{gr}^iP$. It identifies $T$ with $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$ and each $C_{ij}$ with $\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jQ$ in $D(R)$. The theorem's canonicity and second-variable natural transformation identify their morphisms with ordinary tensor maps on these representatives. Consequently the complex comparisons give the displayed natural derived comparisons, with the same identity and composition laws. Only $A_P\le i<B_P$ and $A_Q\le j<B_Q$ have nonzero graded complexes, so every displayed graded sum is a finite biproduct. In the additive derived category with its induced localization structure [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the chain-level summand inclusions and projections still satisfy $p_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\iota_ip_i=1$. These equations exhibit the localization of that complex sum as the direct sum of the localized graded tensors: the map with prescribed components is $\sum_i\iota_if_i$, and uniqueness follows by the second identity. Thus the derived comparison includes the canonical direct-sum identification, not only the separate identifications of its summands. Its naturality follows from the same inclusions and the representative formula already proved.

proof.text: Suppose $u,v$ are filtered quasi-isomorphisms as in the statement. Under Step 4, the degree-$a$ graded map of $\operatorname{Tot}(u\otimes v)$ is the direct sum, for $i+j=a$, of $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{gr}^iu\otimes\operatorname{gr}^jv)$. Factor each summand as $(\operatorname{gr}^iu\otimes1)$ followed by $(1\otimes\operatorname{gr}^jv)$. The first is a quasi-isomorphism by clause (1) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], since both first factors are K-flat; the second is a quasi-isomorphism by clause (3), since its fixed first factor is K-flat. Only finitely many graded pairs are nonzero. Cohomology of this finite direct sum is the sum of its cohomologies, since kernels and images are computed componentwise, so its map is a quasi-isomorphism. This is precisely a filtered quasi-isomorphism under the definition in the statement.
